newsitem.title: USA: U.S., Japan cite 'understandings,' set new air talks.
newsitem.headline: U.S., Japan cite 'understandings,' set new air talks.

text.p: The United States and Japan ended three days of talks on their troubled aviation relations with "understandings" and plan to hold another round soon, the U.S. Transportation Department said on Thursday.

It said the talks "served to deepen our understandings," but cited no progress in the U.S. effort to persuade Japan to honour what it called the Japanese commitment to allow U.S. carriers to fly to airports in Japan and then on to Asian cities.
Washington has said that honouring the commitment is a prerequisite for a new bilateral free market aviation accord.

The department said "we had a meaningful exchange of views," with each side explaining its positions, including the U.S. proposal to agree to an "open skies" agreement that would end restrictions on services by U.S. and Japanese airlines.
It said another round of what it called "informal" talks, and not negotiations, would be held somewhere between Tokyo and Washington "at the earliest convenient opportunity."

There was no immediate report of movement on a complaint by Northwest Airlines Corp. over Japan's refusal to allow it to fly a Seattle-Osaka-Jakarta route as the United States says is allowed under the 1952 U.S.-Japanese accord.
Northwest has said the United States should retaliate for this by denying a Japan Airlines Co. Ltd. request to fly a route from Tokyo to Kona, Hawaii.

Japan has said the 1952 pact heavily favours U.S. carriers by giving three of them -- United Airlines, a unit of UAL Corp., Federal Express Corp. and Northwest -- access to Japan and beyond, but limits U.S. access by Japanese carriers.
However, the United States has said it will not discuss a new "open skies" agreement with Japan until Japan honours its commitments under the existing 1952 agreement.
